# Charter
In compliance with the newly approved City Ordinance No. 1, Series of 2025, which officially supersedes City Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2018, Gordon College affirms its full adherence to the updated directives as mandated by the local government. The institution remains committed to aligning its policies and operations with the latest regulatory framework to ensure a lawful, effective, and community-responsive higher educational institution.

# College Seal
This is the official college seal/logo of Gordon College. This is to be used in legal and formal documents and correspondence of the College. The colors green and yellow signify the community college’s commitment to sustainable development or a development for all generations as it works towards environmental sustainability in its attainment of its vision, mission and goals. “Ulo ng Apo” represents the city of Olongapo where the local Higher Education Institution is based. This symbolizes the ability of its students to lead and make a difference in the community.
The torch illuminates a book which represents the ability to serve as a guiding light for others. It also shows how education is a beacon of light that nurture learning. It is strategically placed beneath the Ulo ng Apo signifying that knowledge must be used, not for knowledge’s sake, but more for the community which includes its stakeholders.
The circular wreath made of interlocking branches and leaves represents the unity and strength of stakeholders and its students who stand among the distinguished scholars the local HEI molded and developed. With the wreath of laurel leaves being a symbol of honor and victory, students, faculty and the leaders of the institution are expected to achieve victory over ignorance while remaining honorable and preserving integrity towards excellence.
The platinum colored shield placed behind the Ulo ng Apo represents the boldness of its students in pursuit of new horizons of unparalleled intellectual success. To remind its students staff and all the members of the institution to be bold and brave enough to explore and seek new opportunities beyond the four corners of the college towards the development of the community they belong to.
Under the shield is the year that Gordon College was founded. This represents the number of years of upholding its values. Three values guide the college, namely: excellence; character and service which shall guide the institutions’ trifocal function of instruction, research and extension.
The logo is in a form of circle, symbolizing the perfect fulfillment of a holistic educational process.

# History of Gordon College
Gordon College was an off-shoot of the Olongapo City Training Center, then a training center for skilled manpower for employment at the former Naval facility of the United States. With the facility’s closure, and the slowing down of demand for skilled workers, City residents shifted to professional courses. The unavailability of affordable tertiary institutions for urban poor sector of the population led the City Government of Olongapo, during the incumbency of Hon. Katherine H. Gordon, then City Mayor, to open the Olongapo City Colleges through City Ordinance no. 9 series of 1999.
Initially, the College offered Bachelor of Science in Accountancy and Bachelor of Science in Computer Studies to 177 enrollees. Additional four-year programs were offered in the succeeding years to accommodate the demand of City residents for other programs.
City Ordinance no. 42 series of 2002 was passed in May 2002, providing a change in the name of Olongapo City Colleges to Gordon College, its present name, in honor of the Gordon family who greatly contributed to the development of the City of Olongapo. In the same year, the College was officially accepted as a member of the Association of Local Colleges and Universities (ALCU).
In 2004, a revision on the legal basis for the creation and operation of Gordon College was made through City Ordinance no. 36 series of 2004. In the same year, the College was granted by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Region III the certificate to operate with autonomy as per provisions of the Local Government Code of 19991. In addition to its undergraduate programs, the College opened its graduate programs in Education, Public Management and Business Administration.
In 2018, City Ordinance No. 07 series of 2018 was passed revising the charter of Gordon College subject to all Legal and Existing Rules and Regulations. This was superseded by City Ordinance No. 01 series of 2025 which was passed in 2025 that equipped Gordon College to expand its horizon for excellence to national and international level.

# Mandate and Function
Gordon College, formerly Olongapo City Colleges, is a local higher education institution established in 1999 under the City Government of Olongapo.
The College operates by virtue of City Ordinance No. 36, Series of 2004 and its amendment City Ordinance No. 1, Series of 2025 also known as the “ 2025 Revised Charter of Gordon College” that supersedes the City Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2018 . The proposed revision of the Charter of Gordon College aims to strengthen the promotion of excellence and delivery of education in the national and international level.
The Local Government of Olongapo supports and maintains its commitment to provide accessible and equitable distribution of opportunities to its constituents to acquire higher education, as well as, a responsive and relevant higher education institution.
### Legal Bases
* **CHED Memorandum Order No. 32, Series of 2006** – Policies, Standards and Guidelines on the Establishment and Operation of Local Colleges and Universities (LCUs);
* **CHED Memorandum Order No. 4, Series of 2007** – Implementing Rules of CM032, Series of 2006;
* **CHED Memorandum Order No. 42, Series of 2016** – Amendment of Article V, Section 5 and 12 of CMO 32, Series of 2006;
* **DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2009-67** – Guidelines on the Establishment of Local Colleges and Universities by Local Governments, and on the Operation of Higher Education Programs;
* **Republic Act No. 7722** – Higher Education Act of 1994;
* **Republic Act No. 9160** – Local Government code of 1991;
* **City Ordinance No. 1, Series of 2025** – 2025 Revised Charter of Gordon College
* **City Ordinance No. 7, Series of 2018** – Revised Charter of Gordon College of 2018;
* **City Ordinance No. 8, Series of 2010** – An Ordinance Amending the Legal Basis on the Creation and Operation of Gordon College;
* **Resolution No. 42, Series of 2002**– A Resolution Chaning the Name of Olongapo City Colleges to “Gordon College”;
* **City Ordinance No. 9, Series of 1999** – An Ordinance Creating Olongapo City Colleges

# Vision, Mission, Objectives, and Core Values
## Vision
A globally recognized local institution committed to innovative academic excellence, holistic and sustainable development, inclusivity, and community engagement.
## Mission
Produce empowered global citizens who create sustainable impact, uphold values of character, excellence, and service, and contribute to academic and societal development
## Strategic Objectives
1. **H**arness partnerships and linkages to produce graduates with global competencies aligned with the needs of the community and industry.
2. **O**rganize extension programs to sustain the greater impact of the institution to the community and environment.
3. **L**everage research outputs to improve existing knowledge and practices.
4. **I**ntegrate ethical principles and standards in the curriculum to strengthen the moral responsibilities of lifelong learners.
5. **S**upport continuous professional development and well-being of employees.
6. **T**ailor-fit student support services to ensure students thrive in the rapidly changing world.
7. **I**nvest in state-of-the-art facilities and technologies to enhance teaching, learning and research.
8. **C**ultivate a culture that embraces diversity and inclusivity.
## Core Values
* **Character.** Character is the foundation of a meaningful life. The institution strives to instill in students a strong moral compass, integrity, and a sense of responsibility for their actions. This includes fostering critical thinking skills, respect for diversity, and a commitment to a lifelong learning.
* **Excellence.** The institution provides a rigorous academic environment that challenges students to reach their full potential. Intellectual curiosity, innovation, and a pursuit of knowledge for its won sake is encouraged. It is believed that excellence is not just about achieving high grades, but also about developing the ability to analyze complex problems, think creatively, and communicate effectively.
* **Service.** Education empowers individuals to make a positive impact on their communities and the world. Students are encouraged to engage in service-learning opportunities that allow them to apply their knowledge and skills to real-world problems. The institution fosters a culture of social responsibility where students develop a sense of compassion and a desire to contribute to the betterment of society.

# Colleges
**Institute of Graduate Studies**
The mission of the Institute of Graduate Studies of Gordon College is to provide quality master’s degree programs and opportunities for continuing professional and career development for students whose academic preparation and personal characteristics foresee success in graduate studies. Each graduate program is firmly grounded in theoretical and empirical bodies of knowledge. Students are challenged to think critically and creatively, and to apply theories to practice in an atmosphere of inquiry and dynamic exchange with faculty and each other
**College of Allied Health Studies**
By 2025, the College of Allied Health Studies is envisioned to be a Center of Excellence in Allied Health Education in Region III and dedicated to being a forerunner in providing research-inclined instruction, evidence-based practice and community–responsive health care education committed to the holistic development of the human person.
**College of Business and Accountancy**
A center of excellence in accounting and business education that develops competitive leaders and professionals for providing professional training, innovative research and relevant extension services.
**College of Computer Studies**
The College of Computer Studies shall be the Center of Excellence in Information Technology and Computer Science for providing professional and technological training, scientific and innovative, and relevant community service
**College of Education, Arts and Sciences**
We envision the Gordon College-College of Education, Arts and Sciences to be a center of excellence in the field for providing professional training, innovative research and community service.
**College of Hospitality and Tourism Management**
To be a center of excellence in tourism and hospitality management with high standard through instruction, research and extension.

# Academic Affairs
Academic affairs is the institutional office that oversees a variety of academic programs and departments at a school. The head of this office supports curriculum initiatives, faculty hiring and promotion events, faculty research and teaching, and all academic departments and programs.

# Continuing Students, Returnees and Cross Enrollment
## Continuing Students and Returnees
Continuing students are those who were previously enrolled in the College but unable to enroll for at least one semester and decided to continue studying in GC. These students have not requested for any transfer credential. They may have or have not filed for Leave of Absence.
Returning students are those who requested for transfer credentials but decided to re-enroll in the College. Returning students shall no longer be required to take the admission test.
## Cross Enrollment
* **GC Students to Enroll in Other Schools**
  + Students shall not be allowed to cross-enroll without proper consultation and consent from their respective College Deans. Students shall not be allowed to cross-enroll if the subject/course is not open during his/her last two semesters in the College. He/She shall request recommendation from his/her Dean and authorization coming from the College Registrar before he/she can cross-enroll to other colleges/universities.
* **Students from Other Schools to Cross-enroll in GC**
  + Students from other schools who would cross-enroll in GC should present a written permission from his school that he/she is allowed to enroll in GC.

# Freshmen Students
## Admission Requirements
Admission to Gordon College shall be open to Filipino citizens, both residents and non-residents of Olongapo City, Non-Filipino citizens, high school graduates, or passers of the high school equivalency certificate (PEPT), and shows evidence of being able to benefit from instruction. A NON-RESIDENT is defined as any individual who has lived less than one year in Olongapo City, is not registered to vote in Olongapo City and/or does not pay property taxes or contributes to the economic development of Olongapo City.
## New College Freshmen Students for Undergraduate Programs
* Admission to the chosen degree program will be based on an applicant’s Gordon College Admission Test (GCAT) results and previous high school/college academic records.
* Original copy of High School Report Card (F138/SF9) or Original ALS Certificate of Rating Secondary Level for ALS Passers
* Certificate of Good Moral Character
* Copy of Birth Certificate
* Medical Certificate (Issued by the Gordon College Clinic)
* Barangay Certificate of Residency
* One 2×2 picture

# IGS (Institute of Graduate Studies) Students
To qualify for admission to the Institute of Graduate Studies, an applicant must meet the following general and specific standards:
1. Student must have a minimum undergraduate GPA of 2.00 or 85% (except NSTP and PE). Student with lower general average than the prescribed rating may be admitted to the master’s program on probation. While on probationary status, s/he is allowed to carry the maximum load of only six (6) units per term. S/he will be placed in full standing status after having obtained an average rating of 1.5 or better in the first 12 units.
2. Specific programs may have different requirement as well as additional requirements such as materials and a personal interview, to wit:
   1. Master in Public Administration
      * At least two (2) years of government/ public service in any capacity
   2. Master in Business Management
      * BS Commerce or BS Business Administration graduate
      * Non-business course graduate must finish 18 tool courses. While earning these units, s/he may enroll any two basic/major subjects in the MBM program.
      * At least two (2) years of relevant experience/ service.
   3. Master of Arts in Education
      * Should be an education graduate
      * For non-education graduate, at least 24 units of professional education in the undergraduate level.
      * At least two (2) years of teaching experience/ service.
   4. Master of Arts in Nursing
      * Should be a Registered Nurse
      * At least two (2) years of experience in nursing and/or related field.
3. Pass the qualifying examination and interview.
4. All applicants for admission must submit the following;
   * Original Transcript of Records from recognized colleges or universities (with remarks, “Copy for Gordon College” or “Granted Honorable Dismissal”).
   * Two ID pictures (2×2/passport size)
   * Certificate of Employment
   * A Php200.00 non-refundable fee for application processing.
   * Additional materials, if required by specific program.

# Student Publication
**The Forefront** is the official student publication of Gordon College located in Olongapo City Sports Complex, Donor Street, East Tapinac, Olongapo City 2200. Its office is located at Rm. 516, 5th Floor, GC Main Building.
The Forefront was reestablished on June 2009, after a four-year hiatus, with the desire to promote the development and growth of responsible journalism as a means of strengthening ethical values, encouraging critical and creative thinking, and developing moral character and personal discipline in accordance with the Campus Journalism Act of 1991 (R.A. 7079).
**THE LOGO**
The official logo of the Forefront, as appeared above, is consist of two elements and two colors.
A *quill or pluma* refers to the writing profession. Its color, red, symbolizes courage and sacrifice. A *stem of laurel leaves* signifies triumph. Its color, golden yellow, symbolizes the nobility of the writing profession. The quill and the stem of laurel leaves form a capital letter “F” which stands for The Forefront.
**General Principles and Objectives**
The Forefront lives with its tagline, **“Informing and Empowering.”** To be able to uphold with its battlecry for campus press freedom, the Editorial Board sets the following General Principles:
1. The Forefront shall serve primarily as a newspaper of and for the students. It shall protect and promote the constitutionally mandated rights of students to free speech and of expression. In addition, it shall protect and promote the students’ rights and welfare.
2. The Forefront, being a publication of the students devoted to the ideals of truth, shall pursue the mission of social transformation through active and responsible journalism.
3. The Forefront, being an independent institution, shall not be subjected to any form of censorship. In turn, the editors and staff shall see to it that the Forefront exercises academic and campus press freedom in accordance with the laws of the Republic of the Philippines. It shall also seek to protect and promote  
   press freedom by taking firm and assertive stance against elements endangering such right.
4. The editors shall respect the rights of other parties that are equally protected by the laws of the Republic of the Philippines, affording them the right and opportunity to refute or reply to criticism or comment hurled at them.
Along with this principles, The Forefront shall at all times strive to:
1. Inform the public (i.e. the general population of the College, including the administration and the general public outside the College) with news of relevance and interest;
2. Serve as a venue for campus opinion and in maintaining an atmosphere of free and responsible discussion and of intellectual exploration;
3. Provide an outlet for students’ suggestions for the betterment of the campus;
4. Develop students’ powers of observation and discrimination concerning relative merits of news articles and;
5. Provide an opportunity for journalistic and creative writing.

# TF’s Luto, among top newsletters at 2026 AOCPA; scribes bag 4 individual awards
[Image: TF’s Luto, among top newsletters at 2026 AOCPA; scribes bag 4 individual awards]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Saturday, March 7, 2026**
he Forefront, the official student publication of Gordon College, took home the 8th Most Outstanding Campus Newsletter and four individual awards at the 6th Assumption Outstanding Campus Press Awards (AOCPA).
The event, hosted by the University of the Assumption’s Regina, took place in San Fernando, Pampanga, on February 27.
The first semestral issue of The Forefront, Luto, was one of this year’s recipients of Most Outstanding Campus Newsletter.
During the awards ceremony, the publication’s Editor-in-Chief John Patrick Mateo earned the 2nd Most Outstanding Campus Journalist award.
Opinion-Editorial Editor Stephanie Estrella’s piece, “Pundido ang ilaw sa susunod na kalsada”, made her the 4th Most Outstanding Editorial Writer and Punto Central Luzon’s Choice for Most Outstanding Editorial Writer.
Meanwhile, Head of Visual Arts Maryisobelle Arcilla was named the 10th Most Outstanding Editorial Cartoonist in another Luzon-wide stint.
The annual awards, featuring 46 publications from various regions in the north, saw The Forefront emerge as one of Luzon’s best.

# GCAAI accepts partnership with Lighthouse Bible Baptist Church and The Great Lighthouse Foundation, Inc
[Image: GCAAI accepts partnership with Lighthouse Bible Baptist Church and The Great Lighthouse Foundation, Inc]
[Alumni](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/alumni/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Monday, December 18, 2023**
In a heartfelt recognition ceremony on December 16, 2023, the Gordon College Alumni Association, Inc. (GCAAI) was honored as one of the Ministry Partner by Lighthouse Bible Baptist Church and The Great Lighthouse Foundation, Inc. This prestigious acknowledgment and appreciation is a testament to the enduring collaboration between the two entities, fostering a spirit of community service and shared impact.
Over the year, GCAAI and Lighthouse Bible Baptist Church have embarked on several community outreach initiatives that go beyond the traditional boundaries of alumni engagement. These collaborative efforts include vital programs such as Basic Life Support Training, Brigada Eskwela Medical Mission, and the Community Wellness and Outreach Program, among others. These endeavors underline the commitment of both organizations to making a positive difference in the lives of the community they serve.
Mr. Joseph Pusing, Vice President of GCAAI, proudly accepted the award on behalf of the association, accompanied by fellow working committee members, Mr. Kenneth Bautista and Ms. Denise Punzalan.
As we express our gratitude for this significant recognition, GCAAI looks forward to further strengthening its partnership with Lighthouse Bible Baptist Church and The Great Lighthouse Foundation, Inc. This accolade not only celebrates past achievements but also serves as a motivation to continue impactful community service initiatives in the future.
GCAAI extends heartfelt thanks to Lighthouse Bible Baptist Church for their continuous support, and we are excited about the prospect of making an even more profound impact on the community through shared vision and collaboration.

# CHED validates the MAN program of Institute of Graduate Studies
[Image: CHED validates the MAN program of Institute of Graduate Studies]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Thursday, June 19, 2025**
The CHED Technical Panel for Nursing, Technical Evaluator for Nursing, and Regional Quality Assessment Team (RQAT) conducted onsite validation at Gordon College, Institute of Graduate Studies, last May 29-30, 2025.
The Gordon College welcomed evaluators from the Commission on Higher Education (CHED)—Regional Quality Assessment Team (RQAT) for an on-site validation aimed at securing a Certificate of Program Compliance (COPC) for the Master of Arts in Nursing (MAN) program.
Program Chair for MAN, Dr. Victor C. Quimen Jr., introduced the CHED-RQAT evaluators: Dr. Maria Martina Geraldine Dimalibot, Dr. Al D. Biag, Dr. Mary Ann Gienette D. Medina, and Ms. Niña Jessa Angeli Palaganas.
The evaluators conducted thorough assessments of program administration, faculty credentials, curriculum, student services, facilities, and resources. Their findings and recommendations, discussed in a post-evaluation conference, will guide Gordon College, Institute of Graduate Studies continuing efforts to enhance academic quality.
Preparations were led by Dr. Imelda DP. Soriano, Dean of the Institute of Graduate Studies; Dr. Darwin P. Paguio, Vice President for Academic Affairs; Dr. Narcisa R. Figuerres, Assistant Dean of the Institute of Graduate Studies; and Dr. Victor C. Quimen Jr. Program Chair for MAN, Ms. Joan Joy A. De Vera; Executive Assistant of the Institute of Graduate Studies, Ms. Diana Grace M. Vallar; Executive Assistant of the Academic Affairs Office; and strong support from other college officials and faculty.
Gordon College, Institute of Graduate Studies, conveyed its sincere gratitude to the CHED-RQAT team for their invaluable insights and steadfast support, recognizing the visit as a major step in the institution’s ongoing journey toward academic excellence.

# LIMC Packed with Students as New School Year Opens
[Image: LIMC Packed with Students as New School Year Opens]
[LIMC](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/limc/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, September 18, 2022**
Welcome Back to School at Gordon College is phenomenal as students spend their spare time inside the library reading books. Students from different departments utilize the library in doing their homework or completing their reading materials. This is highly unexpected because of the recent pandemic.
Since the recent pandemic, Gordon College has implemented a lot of new rules for students to follow in order for them to be safe and healthy. The same goes with the library since it is a place where students get to spend some time studying for their upcoming exams and projects. In fact, students are not allowed to bring food inside the library since not all food are safe to eat anymore because of lack of proper sanitation and hygiene practices during meal preparation.
Despite these new rules being implemented by Gordon College, many students still prefer staying inside the library because it gives them an opportunity to study without any distractions from other people or places around campus.

# GC marks second year in One Billion Rising movement to end violence against women and girls
[Image: GC marks second year in One Billion Rising movement to end violence against women and girls]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Monday, February 16, 2026**
Gordon College marked its second consecutive year of participation in the global campaign One Billion Rising through a public awareness activity themed “Rise for our bodies, our Earth, our Future,” held at Ayala Malls Harbor Point on February 14.  
The event brought together students and mall-goers in a collective call to stand against violence toward women and girls while promoting empowerment and social responsibility.  
Established in 2012, One Billion Rising has developed into an international movement recognized for mobilizing communities across the world to advocate for the elimination of gender-based violence.  
The initiative is grounded in global data from the United Nations indicating that approximately one in three women experience violence at some point in their lives, representing more than a billion women and girls worldwide.  
The activity was led by the Institutional Planning, Development, and External Affairs (IPDEA) through the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Unit in partnership with the National Service Training Program (NSTP) and Ayala Malls Inc., with the goal of strengthening public awareness and encouraging community participation in the advocacy.  
One of the program’s highlights was a flash mob performance by Pase Ballo and SHAPES, who led a mass dance to the One Billion Rising anthem, Break the Chain, symbolizing unity and resistance.  
Mr. Joseph Atencio, head of the DEI Unit, emphasized that violence against women and girls does not only occur in public spaces but is often present within homes and personal relationships.  
“Bukod sa awareness na gusto nating ipakalat, gusto nating maging mapagmatyag ‘yung mga tao. The purpose of One Billion Rising is truly to end violence against women and girls. There can be no sustainable development without women’s empowerment,” he remarked. | via Alyssa Marie Alcantara/The FOREFRONT

[Image: Empowering Solo Parents: Gordon College Launches ‘Weave of Strength’ Initiative]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, April 8, 2026**
Empowering communities through sustainable livelihood and inclusive development, Weave of Strength: Turning Scraps into Sustainable Livelihood was conducted on April 7, 2026 at the Gordon College Function Hall. The initiative provided solo parents and economically disadvantaged individuals with practical skills in transforming recycled fabric scraps into sustainable sources of income.

# Proper Usage of Glass Boards
[Image: Proper Usage of Glass Boards]
**Thursday, May 23, 2024**
GUIDELINES FOR THE USE OF GLASS BOARD INSTALLED IN THE CLASSROOMS
* Use White Board Marker only to write on it
* Always erase marker ink from the surface after each use to prevent stains and ghosting.
* Don’t use dirty eraser or cloth, it will start spread ink residue across the surface of the board.
* Glass board must be cleared of any markings before the next class starts.
* Avoid using tapes or adhesives on the glass surface. These materials may be difficult and cause permanent damage to the glass board.
* Don’t use your hands to wipe a glass board! Your skin carries natural oils that over time leave a build-up of oil residue on the board. This can eventually ruin the surface of the glass board.
* Do not use sharp objects to avoid scratching or damaging the board surface.
* If the glass board is accidentally broken, it must be replaced with the same brand within seven (7) days from the date it was broken. If the item with specific brand and specification is not available, it must be replaced with three (3) timex of the quantity or in quantity comparable to the price of the item. The brand and specification must be approved first by the concerned personnel before replacement.


### Source: https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/announcement/the-4th-gordon-college-distinguished-alumni-service-award-call-for-nomination-2025

# THE 4TH GORDON COLLEGE DISTINGUISHED ALUMNI SERVICE AWARD: Call for Nomination 2025
[Image: THE 4TH GORDON COLLEGE DISTINGUISHED ALUMNI SERVICE AWARD: Call for Nomination 2025]
[Alumni](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/alumni/)
**Monday, August 4, 2025**
**GENERAL INFORMATION AND GUIDELINES**
Pursuant to Gordon College Alumni Association, Inc. (GCAAI) Board Resolution No. 4, series of 2022, the GCAAI establishes the DISTINGUISHED ALUMNI SERVICE AWARD (DASA) to honor Gordon College graduates who have excelled both in their professional and personal careers and who have served as an example to other alumni, students, and the community, both locally and globally. Starting this year, the GCAAI Board of Trustees will recognize the exemplary service and distinguished achievements that brought honor to the Institution and have made significant contributions to society. The GC-DASA recipients will exemplify the core values that the Institution uphold since its establishment: Exceptional Character, Remarkable Excellence, And Unselfish Service.  
The GC-DASA shall be the highest honor bestowed by the Alumni Association and will be an event to be celebrated annually as part of the GC Founding Anniversary and/or GC Alumni Homecoming.  
**GENERAL GUIDELINES:**
1. Only graduates of Gordon College (or GC, formerly Olongapo City Colleges) are eligible for the GC-DASA. The nominee shall be a member of the Gordon College Alumni Association, Inc. as confirmed by its Board.
2. Any GC graduate, faculty member, or stakeholders may make nominations for the GC-DASA. Self–  
   nominations are accepted. The nominee shall accomplish the Official Nomination Form to be provided by the GCAAI. No limitation will be placed on the total number of nominations accepted for consideration.
3. The nominee shall have no pending administrative or criminal case upon nomination. He/she shall exhibit a high degree of character & integrity.
4. Only one recipient per college/program will be awarded. In case the college/program will have no  
   nominees/recipients, the awarding ceremony will still commence. Likewise, the GCAAI Board of Trustees can directly, without prejudice to the respective college, nominate and evaluate for such an award though the college/program have already a candidate.
5. Only living candidates are considered. In the event of the death of a candidate between notification of the award and the award ceremony, the award may be given posthumously with the permission of the family and the GCAAI. In the event that the awardee declines to accept the award and/or fails to attend the awarding ceremonies, the GCAAI reserves the right to withdraw the award.
6. A GC graduate sitting as a member of the selection committee or a member of the GCAAI Board of Trustees is not eligible to receive the award. This individual is eligible for nomination after a one-year waiting period from the date he/she steps down from his/her role.
7. Recipients are only eligible for one GC-DASA in a lifetime.
8. The recipients will receive a plaque or certificate of recognition and will be posted on the official FB page of the GCAAI. It will announce the annual recipients through various methods and honor each recipient with the appropriate recognition.
9. If for any reason, the GCAAI is not able to conduct the Awards as planned (including due to tampering, unauthorized intervention, fraud, technical difficulties, pandemic, or any other causes beyond the control of the organizer which impact the administration, security, fairness, integrity or proper conduct of the Awards), then they reserve the right in their sole discretion to make any reasonable variation to the Awarding Ceremony.
10. The Nomination Committee and/or GCAAI Board of Trustees may disqualify any nominee that they  
    reasonably determine has breached any of the terms and conditions or otherwise engaged in unlawful or other improper conduct that may bring the Awards into disrepute or jeopardize the fair and proper conduct of the Awards.
11. Other guidelines may be promulgated as decided by the GCAAI Board of Trustees.
**NOMINATION COMMITTEE:**  
The Nomination Committee (NC) may be organized by the Dean/OIC in every college and/or the GCAAI. The committee must be composed of at least three (3) members from their respective colleges. The total count of committee members should be an odd number. The chairperson of the NC shall be the Dean or its duly authorized representative and for the GCAAI, any member can initiate such nomination. No member of the NC must be related within the second degree of consanguinity or affinity to any of the nominees/candidates for awards. If the Dean/OIC is related within the second degree of consanguinity or affinity to any of the candidates for awards, the Dean/OIC must inhibit him/herself from participating in the process. The approval shall come from the person next in rank.  
The NC shall:
1. Abide by the criteria set forth by the GCAAI.
2. For nominees endorsed by the College, it shall issue a certificate of authenticity to all the documents that will be submitted to the GCAAI.
3. Deliberate on the qualifications of the nominees for the awards based on the criteria and the documents submitted.
4. Recommend to the GCAAI Board of Trustees or its Alumni Association President the result of nomination for approval.
5. Recommend to the GCAAI Board of Trustees or its Alumni Association President the resolution on any related issue that may arise from the results of the awards.
6. Ensure that the guidelines stipulated herein are followed.
**NOMINATION AND SELECTION PROCESS:**
1. Complete the online/hard copy Nomination Form.
2. Nominators will receive an auto-generated copy via email of what they submitted, i.e., the nomination form including any attachments. In any case, it is not available, the NC may determine what means of notification it will conduct to the nominators to confirm the submission of the nomination form and its attachments.
3. Nominees and nominators will be contacted by the NC/GCAAI within three days of receipt of the  
   nomination to acknowledge receipt.
4. A nominee may be asked to clarify or submit further information and evidence to assist the NC/GCAAI in assessing the nomination at any stage of the selection process.
5. The NC/GCAAI may also seek verification of the nominee’s achievements from their current or previous employer or other relevant individual or organization representative. By being nominated for this Award, the nominees are giving consent to the NC/GCAAI to contact these individuals to verify nominations.
6. Nominations will be reviewed and shortlisted by the NC/GCAAI and nominees who have not been  
   shortlisted will be notified. The GC-DASA candidates will be asked to submit a brief profile for this purpose. The candidate shall garner a total score of 60 points to be included in the shortlist. If a nominee cannot meet the required points, he/she is automatically excluded from the shortlist.
7. Every member of the NC will recommend/endorse the final candidate to the GCAAI President and then, the GCAAI Board of Trustees, sitting as Awards Selection Committee, will issue a confirmation through a Board Resolution. The report on the results of the NC shall be signed by all members of the committee and certified by the chairperson.
8. In any case that such protest will be filed during the confirmation of the final candidates, the final decision on the protest shall be decided by the GCAAI Board of Trustees. The GCAAI Board of Trustees’ decision is final on all matters relating to the nomination process and the selection of award recipients, and they are not required to provide feedback as to why a nomination was unsuccessful.
Call for Nominations: 4th Distinguished Alumni Service Award (DASA)
The Gordon College Alumni Association, Inc. proudly announces the opening of nominations for the 4th Distinguished Alumni Service Award (DASA), which will run from August 4 to 22, 2025. This prestigious recognition honors outstanding alumni who have demonstrated exceptional service, leadership, and commitment to their profession, community, or alma mater. We encourage all alumni, faculty, and stakeholders to submit nominations for individuals who embody the values and excellence upheld by Gordon College. For complete nomination guidelines, kindly scan the QR code below.
The awarding ceremony will be held on October 11, 2025. Let us come together to recognize and celebrate the achievements of Gordon College alumni who continue to make a lasting difference.

# BASURA, PASILIDAD, UNIPORME: Students Address Concerns In Town Hall Meeting
[Image: BASURA, PASILIDAD, UNIPORME: Students Address Concerns In Town Hall Meeting]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Tuesday, November 11, 2025**
GORDON COLLEGE FUNCTION HALL MAIN BLDG—In an effort to strengthen transparency and communication between the student body and the administration, various students and representatives from different organizations voice out their concerns and proposed solutions on pressing campus issues that affect their daily experiences on the Town Hall Meeting, spearheaded by the Supreme Student Council (SSC) of Gordon College (GC) on November 4, at Gordon College Function Hall Main Bldg.
Among the major issues discussed were concerns with the disappearance of trash bins, restroom malfunctions, and the absence of student lounges, which reflect the everyday struggles of GCians that often go unnoticed. While these may seem like small matters, they collectively define the comfort, cleanliness, and morale of the student body.
Meanwhile, other pressing matters, such as the condition of the main and annex buildings and inconsistent implementation of the dress code, point to deeper issues of transparency, inclusivity, and student welfare.
DISAPPEARANCE OF TRASH BINS: CLEANLINESS AND WASTE MANAGEMENT ISSUES RAISED
Campus cleanliness had been a pressing issue among students following the recent disappearance of trash bins across campus. Students reported that many areas, including restrooms, now lack accessible waste bins, leading to increased littering and cleanliness issues.
Participants suggest restoration of the trash bins throughout the campus to promote cleanliness and for students’ easier access, emphasizing that this could help maintain a clean environment around the campus.
BUILDING FUNCTIONALITY: CALLS FOR BETTER FACILITIES BOTH IN THE MAIN AND ANNEX BUILDINGS
Moreover, the Annex Building, which accommodates a growing number of classes, points to another major concern. Students described poor ventilation, unstable internet connectivity, and a lack of proper equipment—including the sound system in the Function Room—as recurring problems that lessen their productivity.
Furthermore, students also expressed frustrations over the lack of equipment in the Main Building, such as practicums and simulations.
The SSC noted the importance of these concerns and emphasized the need for facility upgrades to ensure a more conducive academic environment, emphasizing that as Gordon College aims to be a university, infrastructure and facility improvements must keep pace with academic demands.
DRESS CODE VIOLATIONS: STUDENTS CALL FOR CONSISTENCY AND CLARITY
One of the most discussed topics was the implementation of the college’s dress code policy. Several students expressed confusion over inconsistent enforcement across departments, citing instances of inconsistency and a lack of clear communication throughout the student body.
“Minsan po navi-violation kami kahit appropriate po ‘yung suot namin [na uniform],” one Bachelor of Science and Tourism Management (BSTM) Student expressed.
Participants also noted that some students are reprimanded for minor violations while others are not held to the same standard.
“Naka-org shirt po ako then ni-question po ako kung bakit [naka-org shirt]. Nag-explain po ako na may event, pero may nauna po sakin na naka-civilian [pero] ‘di po siya ni-question,” another student from College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS) shared.
In the latter part of the meeting, Gcians requested clearer guidelines and a more uniform implementation across departments to help promote both discipline and inclusivity within the campus community, and avoid misunderstanding and unequal treatment.
STUDENT LOUNGE, RESTROOM, AND OTHER CONCERNS
The functionality and cleanliness of restrooms were also brought up as a long-standing concern. Some facilities were reported to have malfunctioning faucets and dysfunctional doors, toilets, and bidets. Students cite concerns for regular maintenance checks to ensure comfort and hygiene for all.
On the other hand, Participants also voiced out frustrations over the lack of student lounges and rest areas where they can relax, study, or collaborate during vacant periods. Many pointed out that the few available classrooms require permission to be used, forcing students to stay in hallways or stairwells in between classes.
One student from CHTM proposed designating student lounges on each floor to provide space for students as a resolution, citing that this would provide comfort for students.
The SSC assured attendees that all issues and recommendations raised will be compiled and formally addressed to the college administration for further deliberation with the BIBINGKA project, held on November 7, Friday.
The council also promised its commitment to continue facilitating such dialogues to ensure that students’ voices are not only heard but also acted upon. | via Love Lorraine Acedo/The FOREFRONT

# GC presents one thousand students in graduation rites
[Image: GC presents one thousand students in graduation rites]
[Campus](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/campus/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Thursday, July 10, 2025**
Gordon College’s (GC) 23rd Commencement Exercises saw a total of 1,016 passionate graduates walk in the aisle of Subic Bay Exhibition and Convention Center (SBECC) this year, donning their respective togas and sablays.
Amidst heavy rains, Cluster I filled the morning ceremony with 487 graduates from the College of Business and Accountancy (CBA) and Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM).
Meanwhile, 529 students from Cluster II’s College of Allied Health Sciences (CAHS), College of Computer Studies (CCS), and College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS) graced the stage during the afternoon rites.
The graduates are products of Free Higher Education (FHE) from the institution and taxpayers, who enjoyed it during their tenure.

# GCAAI Membership
#### Qualifications for Membership
A. The qualifications for membership to the Association are either:
1. Holder of academic degree from Gordon College (formerly Olongapo City Colleges)
2. Holder of secondary/basic education diploma from Gordon College-Senior High School
3. Holder of academic title or postgraduate diploma from Gordon College (formerly Olongapo City Colleges)
4. Not having been dismissed for misconduct/offenses or scholastic/academic deficiency which is automatically considered not a member of the Association.
B. Membership to the association may be bestowed upon the approval of the GC-AA Board of Trustees:
1. Holders of honorary degrees from the College;
2. Former or current members of the faculty and staff of the College who have rendered service to the College for at least ten (10) years.
C. Active members are those who have qualified as members under Section 1 and 2, and are either:
1. Members who have paid lifetime membership dues;
2. Members who have paid and are up-to-date in their annual membership dues;
3. Members who have participated in such other programs that sustain, develop, and promote the Association’s objectives as determined by the Board.
D. The Alumni Oath shall be recited by a member who signifies its willingness to be part of and reflect its allegiance to the Association. The Alumni Oath shall be administered by the President or its duly authorized representative in a ceremony, commencement and/or event. The Alumni Oath in its current form is as follows:
*I **(state your name)**,*  
*a graduate of Gordon College,*  
*hereby undertake to*  
*vigilantly upholds the ideals*  
*and shield the honor of my Alma Mater,*  
*and as a fulfilled member of the Gordon College Alumni Association, Inc.,*  
*will uphold its Constitution and By-Laws,*  
*to remain a true paragon towards excellence,*  
*committed to do justice to everyone*  
*in service to our country and our God.*  
*So help me, God!*

# GC ALAB 2026: Connecting Job Seekers to Opportunities on GC’s 27th Anniversary
[Image: GC ALAB 2026: Connecting Job Seekers to Opportunities on GC’s 27th Anniversary]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, February 25, 2026**
In celebration of the 27th Founding Anniversary, the GC ALAB Job Fair was successfully conducted on February 25, 2026, at Ayala Malls Harbor Point – Activity Center from 9:00 AM to 3:00 PM.
The event was spearheaded by the Public Employment Service Office (PESO) in collaboration with Gordon College, particularly under the Community Extension Unit and the Office of Student Welfare and Services, as part of the institution’s commitment to serving its stakeholders by providing accessible employment opportunities.
A total of 30 participating companies joined the job fair, offering various career opportunities for job seekers and fresh graduates.
This meaningful activity was made possible through the partnership of Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), SBMA Labor, Ayala Malls Harbor Point, JPMAP, SMAP, and the College of Business and Accountancy.
The GC ALAB Job Fair reflects Gordon College’s dedication to community extension and workforce development.

# Website Policy
### Website Committee
Gordon College (GC) Website Committee was formally established by Interoffice Memorandum No. 38 Re: Website Committee. The Interoffice Memorandum states the following; composition, duties, and responsibilities of Website Committee, Guidelines in Website Content Development and Management, and Procedure for Posting/Uploading Web Content.
### Composition
GC Website Committee will be composed of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Website Administrator, and Members.  
For the members, it will be the Head of the Information and Communication Services Unit (ICSU), one (1) faculty member from each department designated by the College Dean, and one (1) staff from each office/unit assigned by the Unit Head.
### Duties and Responsibilities of Website Committee
Based on Interoffice Memo No. 38, the following are the duties and responsibilities of the committee:
1. Develop and recommend web related policies and standards
2. Oversee the design and underlying technology
3. Ensure the website stays current with new technology/trends
4. Implement regular data collection methods
5. Use data collected to guide the framework and infrastructure of the college website
6. Create guiding principles to steer the framework and infrastructure decisions of the college website
7. Work with the Management Information System Unit (MISU) to set timelines for web engine upgrade and new website deployments.
8. Regularly assess the design of the website and make recommendations for improvement
9. Serve as the liaison between the College President and the different department regards content
10. Identify and advocate for web needs and services for the college community.
### Guidelines in Website Content Development and Management
1. Interoffice Memo No. 38, clearly states the guidelines to be observed by the committee in terms of the contents for the website.
2. All news, updates and all other content to be posted on the official website should have clearance from concerned departments/ units and approval from the College President.
3. The Website Committee is tasked to manage the postings on the official website in coordination with the Information and Communication Services Unit (ICSU). The committee shall formulate posting guidelines and ensure proper dissemination.
4. Queries, concerns or issues aired through the official website must be communicated to concerned departments through ICSU who shall also responsible for posting official responses to such queries, concerns or issues whether through online or offline as the situation warrants.
### Procedure for Posting/Uploading Web Content
The following are the guidelines stated in Interoffice Memo No. 38 in terms of posting/uploading content to the college website:
1. Requesting department should submit a copy of the post to ICSU for approval of the College President.
2. After approval, ICSU shall transmit the content to the Website Committee Chairperson and Web Administrator.
### Website Content Submission
The GC Website Committee is pleased to offer the opportunity to share knowledge and expertise by submitting content to the college website with the following guidelines:
* **Guiding Principles**  
  Gordon College is one of the institutions that promote excellent education in Region III and the country. As such, the committee would like to publish and post content, materials, and ideas that support the vision, mission, and goals of the college. The committee also encourages each individual from different colleges and departments to share their experience and insights as one of the people of Gordon College.
* **Style**  
  The Website committee encourages each and everyone to use the current best practices for web writing. These includes:
  + Begin with the conclusion by focusing on the main message and be clear on how you want the reader to feel and respond.
  + Add specific details, facts, figures, quotes, etc.
  + Submit at least one (1) graphs, graphics, or photos that are copyright free with a size of;
    - 1280 pixels by 720 pixels for Hero Banners (Congratulatory Posters)
    - 1200 pixels by 630 pixels for News, Announcement and Notice
    - 250 pixels by 250 pixels for Website Banner
    - 250 pixels by 100 pixels for Logo (Rectangle)
    - 100 pixels by 100 pixels for Logo (Square)
  + Graphs, graphics or photos should be in .jpeg, .png or .svg format
  + Use subheadings that reflect the content and captures the interests of readers
  + Use listed points with ten (10) words or less per item
  + Search the web for other pro tips on best practices
* **Publishing**  
  The committee does not guarantee that it will post your submissions automatically. All published contents shall be well-guided and must receive the approval of concerned departments, as stated on Interoffice Memorandum No. 38.It does guarantee, however, that the article will be read and explore whether or not it is a good fit for the college and the readership. In reviewing submissions, the committee is looking for content that is necessary and relevant to the needs of the stakeholders, especially with the faculty and students. Articles reflecting the inspiring, powerful, responsible, productive, and connected nature of the academe are the ones that we are looking for.
* **Copyright**  
  The committee will only post copyright-free materials submitted by the author and will not pay for articles posted on the website. The college reserves the right to use the submitted article or any part of it depending on the committee’s discretion.
* **Response Time**  
  The goal of the committee is to respond to the requestor as quickly as possible. Depending on the situation, the committee will do its best to respond to each submission in 1 to 3 days.
* **Requestor**  
  The following groups and/or individuals are allowed to submit content for posting:
  + Department Heads
  + Vice Presidents
  + Faculty Members and
  + Administrative Staff
  + Recognized Student Organizations
  + Alumni
### Specific Guidelines
To achieve uniformity and establish the visual identity of the college kindly follow the following in submitting your content;
* **Title and Author Information**  
  All submission must identify (to be written in the body of your message);
  + Topic
  + Title
  + Author’s Full name
  + Author’s Phone Number\*
  + Author’s Email Address\*
  + Department (if applicable)  
    *\* – needed for communication purposes*
* **Summary**  
  Provide a 20-30 words summary of the article that can be used for links.
* **Length of the Content**  
  Submit articles that are between 500-750 words. Please submit final drafts that have proofread, and grammar and spelling checked.  
  Do not include the graphics or photos within the document. It should be saved separately in the same folder where the file resides.
* **Formatting**  
  Send your document at **biron.neilmarc@gordoncollege.edu.ph** with the following format details:
  + Subject : Request for Posting (Website)
  + Body : Author’s Information
  + Topic : Event/ Celebration
  + Title : Sportsfest
  + Author’s Full name : Juan Dela Cruz
  + Author’s Phone Number : 607.7175
  + Author’s Email Address : juandelacruz@gmail.com
  + Department : College of Allied Health Studies
  + Summary of your article.
  + Attachment:
    - document file of your article
    - picture1.jpg\* / picture1.png\* / picture1.svg\*  
      *\* – you can select one particular image type*
* **Links**  
  Provide a list of referenced links in the text or at the end of the submitted article. The committee will review these links to determine if they are appropriate for the website and will determine if they will be included or not (especially for copyright acknowledgment).
* **Categorization of Submission**  
  Articles that will be posted in the website can be categorized into;
  + News
  + Announcement or Guidelines
  + Notice or Advisory
* **Tags**  
  This will be use to sub-categorized your submission;
  + CAHS *(College of Allied Health Studies)*
  + CCS *(College of Computer Studies)*
  + CBA *(College of Business and Accountancy)*
  + CEAS *(College of Education, Arts, and Sciences)*
  + CHTM *(College of Hospitality and Tourism Management)*
  + IGS (*Institute of Graduate Studies)*
  + OSWS*(Office of Student Welfare and Services)*
  + Campus
  + Alumni
  + Administration
  + Academics
  + Forefront
### Content Administration
All web content submitted must be approved prior to posting. The following individuals retain the right to edit or request changes:
* College President
* Website Administrator
* Head of ICSU
* Vice Presidents
* Requestor/Author of the Content
### Website Content Update/ Revision
Thou postings are checked for spelling, grammar and factual accuracy, there will be some instances that can result unwanted errors.
The GC Website Committee will allow update or revision of articles posted on the website for the following reasons;
* Missing or Duplicate Titles
* Misspelled names
* Overlooked misspelled words or grammatical errors
* Missing images or links
* Missing details or information
### Website Content Removal
The GC Website Committee reserves the right to remove any posted content that contains copyrighted materials which include, but not limited to: text, images, graphics, sound recordings, video recordings or software programs.

# CEAS Mentors Duo Reclaims Gold, Overpowers CBA in Mixed Doubles Badminton Clash
[Image: CEAS Mentors Duo Reclaims Gold, Overpowers CBA in Mixed Doubles Badminton Clash]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, September 17, 2025**
TRICKSHOT COVERED COURT—In a smashing display of speed, precision, and teamwork, the College of Education, Arts and Sciences (CEAS) Mentors reclaimed badminton glory, dominating the mixed doubles championship against the College of Business and Accountancy (CBA) Wizards on September 16, 2025, at the Trickshot Badminton Court.
Right from the opening serve, the dynamic duo of Daniel Ruzzel Bernal and Mary Anne Lafuente wasted no time asserting their dominance with lightning-quick reflexes and razor-sharp shot placements.
Consequently, their rapid-fire rallies and clever net play kept the CBA Wizards scrambling across the court, ending the first set in convincing fashion at 21-9, with CEAS clearly in control.
Building on that first-set momentum, Bernal and Lafuente came out swinging in the second set, smashing their way to an early lead through seamless communication and smart positioning.
Meanwhile, although the Wizards attempted a comeback with aggressive clears and pushes, every move was countered by the Mentors’ calculated drop shots, steady defense, and powerful smashes, closing the set at 21-1 to secure the championship crown.
After the final rally, Lafuente emphasized that the victory was not only a triumph of skill but also a testament to their trust in each other, both on and off the court.
Similarly, Bernal expressed his pride and excitement after clinching the gold, saying, “Sobrang saya po and super proud po ako sa partner ko.”
Before reaching the finals, the duo battled past the CHTM Sharks in the elimination round, overcoming sharp smashes and relentless returns to secure a 30–10 win and a spot in the championship stage.
Furthermore, the CEAS pair showed that age and experience were no barriers, as their first match as college students turned into a golden opportunity to prove their fire and determination. | via Lovely Mae M. Doroin/The FOREFRONTFOREFRONT

# Fostering Mental Health
[Image: Fostering Mental Health]
[Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/extension/) [RDCES](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/rdces/) [Community Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/community-extension/)
**Wednesday, July 26, 2023**
In adherence to our commitment to community service, the GC Community Extension Services Unit (GC-CESU), in collaboration with the GC Guidance Office and Tapinac Senior High School, successfully organized and conducted a seminar on July 31, 2023. The seminar aimed to enhance the resilience of the attendees by equipping them with techniques to address and manage challenges, emphasizing the importance of self-care, addressing mental health stigma, and facilitating access to mental health services. Ms. Mechel Bautista, GC Guidance Office Head, served as the resource speaker. The seminar saw active participation from 42 teachers from Tapinac Senior High School and took place at the Gordon College function hall.

# GC marks a milestone in ALCUCOA 2025
[Image: GC marks a milestone in ALCUCOA 2025]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, December 3, 2025**
The three-day program comes to an end as Gordon College (GC) conducts an exit conference for the Association of Local Colleges and Universities Commission on Accreditation (ALCUCOA) last November 28, at the Gordon College Main Building, Function Hall.
Vying for one Level III program, five Level II programs, and two candidate programs this year, the institution’s big step is a leap for development, embodying character, excellence, and service along the way.
“This is not the end,” Dr. Imelda DP. Soriano opened the exit conference of this year’s accreditation with a firm statement.
The accreditors commended the institution’s strengths including the Library Ambassadors Organization (LAO), community extension programs, and professionalism.
Meanwhile, they also recommended improvements such as stronger programs to supplement both students’ and teachers’ needs, more tangible and sustainable community extensions, and subjects that focus on application rather than theories.
As Dr. Elizabeth Montero, the supervising accreditor said in her message, “The new oil now is consistency,” a reminder to stay true and stand into the lenses of continuous development where growth is evident and seen.
In response, Ms. Geraldine Raydanas and Mrs. Rowenalyn Sagun expressed their utmost gratitude and promised to improve in the areas mentioned.
Ending the program, Dr. Kristin Joy Mendoza, secretary of GC’s Board of Trustees, left a valuable statement regarding institutionalization and sustainability.
“Every accreditation is an opportunity to innovate and fill the spaces where we can do better,” Dr. Mendoza emphasized.
Meanwhile, the results of the 2025 accreditation are set to be announced in the next few weeks. | via Mikhaela Sagun/The FOREFRONT

# TF marks history at 21st LHEPC; 3 scribes snatch indiv awards
[Image: TF marks history at 21st LHEPC; 3 scribes snatch indiv awards]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, March 22, 2026**
The Forefront (TF) delegates secured three individual awards, first time in the publication’s Luzon-wide stint, at the 21st Luzon-Wide Higher Education Press Conference (LHEPC) from March 17-19, at NGN Grand Hotel in Tuguegarao City.
Representing Central Luzon, the individual category participants bagged awards in: Traditional Literary Graphics Illustration (English), 3rd place, from Senior Layout Artist Angelique Jose; Head of Traditional Arts Mary Isobelle Arcilla secured 7th Place in Traditional Comic Strip Drawing (English); and John Christian Rocero, former social media manager, took home 9th place in Photojournalism (English).
At the same time, John Patrick Mateo, Editor-in-Chief, participated in Devcomm Writing (Filipino) while Lance Isaac Leon, Associate Editor, participated in Editorial Writing (English) and Column Writing (English).
Moreover, Region III was named the Best Performing Region for the Individual and Group categories.
Announced on the same day, LHEPC will be replaced next year by the 1st National Higher Education Press Conference (NHEPC), to be hosted by Region I at Vigan City.
Similar to LHEPC rules, the top 5 placers in each category from the respective regional presscons will advance to the NHEPC. | via Roi Chester B. Manio/ THE FOREFRONT

# LCUAA 2025 Welcomes Rainy Sunday Afternoon
[Image: LCUAA 2025 Welcomes Rainy Sunday Afternoon]
[LCUAA](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/lcuaa/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, October 19, 2025**
The eagerly anticipated week-long 14th LCUAA National Games officially kicked off today at the City of San Jose del Monte (CSJDM) Sports Complex.
Cheers and applause filled the venue as the opening ceremony began with a parade featuring all 27 participating colleges, each led by their institution’s gold medalists.
Following the parade was the introduction of the LCUAA 2025 representative officers, a doxology by the Sining Tanglawan ng San Jose del Monte Performing Group, the singing of the National Anthem and the San Jose del Monte city hymn, and an energetic dance performance by the San Joseño World Class Talents troupe.
City College of San Jose del Monte (CCSJDM) College President Dr. Roger S. Ambida delivered the opening remarks, warmly welcoming delegates to the institution.
Hon. Arturo B. Robes then gave the keynote address, encouraging athletes to build a brighter and more empowered future.
Additionally, Dr. Lora L. Yusi, CHED Region 3 Director IV, gave an inspiring speech, highlighting the significance of LCUAA 2025 as a testament to the growth of local universities: “We see scholars who dream larger than themselves.”
The competitive events officially begin tomorrow, October 20, 2025.
Stay tuned to the official Facebook page of The Forefront for updates on the 14th LCUAA National Games. | via Alyssa Marie Alcantara / The FOREFRONT

# GC Welcomes 5 new Registered Midwifes, Perfect passing in November MLE
[Image: GC Welcomes 5 new Registered Midwifes, Perfect passing in November MLE]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, November 19, 2025**
Five alumni from the College of Allied Health and Services (CAHS) of Gordon College (GC) passed the Midwives Licensure Exam (MLE) according to the Professional Regulation Commission Board.
GC achieved a perfect passing rate of 100% with 5 passers out of 5 examinees, once again surpassing the rate of last year’s results of 93.48% and the national rate of 57.60%. They constitute the 2,152 newly registered midwives.
All are first-time takers of this year’s exam.
Additionally, Tagaloan Community College is the top-performing school in the licensure exam with a perfect passing rate from 85 examinees of the school.
Meanwhile, Princesa Dumale Talamayan, this year’s board topnotcher, from Palawan State University achieved a 94.00%.
The licensure exam was held on November 8-9 and 16. | via Roi Chester B. Manio/The FOREFRONT

# RESCHEDULING OF ID PROCESSING (December 8, 2025)
[Image: RESCHEDULING OF ID PROCESSING (December 8, 2025)]
**Sunday, December 7, 2025**
[Image: 📢]
**NOTICE: RESCHEDULING OF ID PROCESSING**
Please be informed that the scheduled ID Processing on December 8, 2025 (Monday) has been rescheduled due to the non-working holiday.   
ID Processing will now be conducted on any day from December 9 to December 12, 2025 (Tuesday–Friday). Students may proceed on their preferred date within this period.   
We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your understanding.

# GC Coastline Clean-up Drive
[Image: GC Coastline Clean-up Drive]
[Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/extension/) [RDCES](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/rdces/) [Community Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/community-extension/)
**Friday, June 23, 2023**
On World Water Day 2023, numerous individuals joined forces with a shared goal of cleaning up the coast to protect nature and ensure clean water. This initiative served as a reminder of the importance of water conservation and environmental preservation. The GC Community Extension Services Unit (GC-CESU) and the Office of Student Welfare and Services (OSWS) partnered with student groups to organize and carry out the cleanup. Their efforts inspired 182 student leaders, volunteers, and advisors to actively participate. Thanks to their enthusiastic involvement, the event was a resounding success.

# ONLINE ADMISSION AND SCREENING PROCESS (First Semester, A.Y. 2024-2025)
[Image: ONLINE ADMISSION AND SCREENING PROCESS (First Semester, A.Y. 2024-2025)]
**Monday, May 13, 2024**
STEP 1. UPLOAD ACADEMIC RECORDS
After taking the Gordon College Admission Test (GCAT), applicants should upload academic records on the GCA portal for screening and evaluation.
1.1) Log-on to the GCA portal ([https://gordoncollegeccs.edu.ph/apps/gca/student](https://gordoncollegeccs.edu.ph/apps/gca/student?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTAAAR2JmPaGUyOVt0YylzcZpGk7_MKmJIRNUTeR_kixe9sO81kSDORJDjpZFS8_aem_Ac1hbmvkRpPsnmngvolehq6C4e6Fh--p9yLqRycCxSskrQCbsht--eGnMI99fQ0EYqAVhIdHG9H6lg7x-UlWbBWj)).
1.2) On the Menu, click “Uploads”
1.3) Upload scanned or clear image of one of the following documents, whichever is applicable:
A. Graduating Grade 12 students
– Grade 12 – FIRST SEMESTER Report Card (SF9)
B. Senior High School Graduates
– Complete HS Report Card (SF9)
C. High School Graduates of Old Basic Education Curriculum (BEC)
– Complete High School Report Card(F-138)
D. Passers of ALS Program
– Alternative Learning System (ALS) Certificate of Completion
E. Transferees
– Official Transcript of Records or Certificate of Grades
Important:
– Applicants who have complete academic records will be prioritized
– Failure to upload academic records will result to cancellation of application
– Applicants are advised to regularly check their GCA portal account for updates.
STEP 2. INTERVIEW
The result of GCAT and previous academic records will be evaluated based on the admission policy of the applied program.
For qualified applicants, a schedule of interview will be posted in the GCA portal. The following are the description of the application status:
a) 1st Choice On going evaluation, means applicant is currently being reviewed in the program you specified as your first choice.
b) 2nd Choice On going evaluation, means applicant is currently being reviewed in the program you specified as your second choice.
c) Accepted, means applicant is qualified for the chosen program and should confirm admission.
d) NOT Accepted, means applicant did not meet the minimum requirement of the program and has been denied in the chosen programs.
e) Confirmed, means applicant have confirmed admission in the program.
f) Declined, means applicant have declined admission in the program. Applicants are encouraged to have alternative plans in case they are not admitted.
STEP 3. CONFIRMATION OF ADMISSION
3.1) Admitted students should confirm their admission FIVE (5) days after the approval of application.
3.2) To confirm admission, on the GCA portal dashboard, click “CONFIRM” button.
STEP 4. SET AN APPOINTMENT FOR SUBMISSION OF REQUIREMENTS
4.1) Log-on to the GCA portal, click Set Appointment Menu.
4.2) Hard copies of the following should be submitted to the Office of the Registrar on the scheduled appointment:
a.1) For Senior High School Graduates -> Original Grade 12 Report Card (SF9)
a.2) For High School Graduates of Old Curriculum -> Original High School Report Card(F-138)
a.3) For Passers of ALS Program -> (ALS) Certificate of Completion
a.4) For Transferees -> Original Official Transcript of Records, Cert. of Eligibility to Transfer/Honorable Dismissal and Good Moral Character Certificate
b) Fully Accomplished Student Information Sheet with 2×2 Picture (white background)
c) Original Recent Certificate of Residency
d) Copy of NSO / PSA Authenticated Birth Certificate
e) Copy of any Valid ID Card / Senior High School ID Card
f) Copy of Medical Certificate issued by the College Clinic
STEP 5. ONLINE ENLISTMENT FOR ENROLMENT
Please visit our official Facebook page for the schedule and process of online enlistment for enrolment for newly admitted students. [https://www.facebook.com/GordonCollegeOfficial](https://www.facebook.com/GordonCollegeOfficial?__cft__[0]=AZVvaXkFZ4kAMff-sbynBKdQ8jebAfiJkp90Rm0Tx3ZWf7F5MngjIhGL5wol1-qHLPQGvEz-8VbixXgKEMvgaWFyAmnNAE5FGHnIPXXODKXiSad_14K0LxfcGQv9gI2VkAJOF5lGCTenhIU52G8euMW-vF1w_Q1K_P6BM4YVJJXnkWrbyPYwpawDKHqARtY-ZgyeTBFg5D5t5aqvr_2BXrA9&__tn__=-]K-R)

# Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Awareness Campaign
[Image: Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Awareness Campaign]
[Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/extension/) [RDCES](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/rdces/) [Community Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/community-extension/)
**Monday, March 13, 2023**
The successful execution of earthquake and fire prevention simulation exercises is essential for reducing risks and enhancing disaster preparation. These simulations play an essential role in strengthening the resilience of communities and organisations in the face of earthquakes and fires. These sessions were successfully carried out owing to the committed efforts of CESU coordinators, admin/faculty volunteers as facilitators, and our resource speakers, Ms. Jerica Baccay (Head of GC DRRMU) and Mr. Jun Ecleo (GC Safety Officer).

# Mentors did not give up on the violent carry of Sharks
[Image: Mentors did not give up on the violent carry of Sharks]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, September 19, 2025**
The College of Education, Arts, and Sciences (CEAS) Mentors brought home the championship for Men’s Futsal against the College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) Sharks with a score of 1-0.
Only in the first seven the battle of the two teams has become a center, thrilled to bring home the gold in their respective departments.
Everyone held their breath in the opposition of the two teams to secure the championship.
Although it wasn’t easy, the Mentors still insisted on bringing out full force to unite with the Sharks.
At the end, the resilience of CEAS Mentors still prevailed and won the battle.

# 𝘼 𝙇𝙚𝙜𝙖𝙘𝙮 𝙤𝙛 𝙀𝙭𝙘𝙚𝙡𝙡𝙚𝙣𝙘𝙚, 𝘼 𝙁𝙪𝙩𝙪𝙧𝙚 𝙤𝙛 𝙄𝙢𝙥𝙖𝙘𝙩
[Image: 𝘼 𝙇𝙚𝙜𝙖𝙘𝙮 𝙤𝙛 𝙀𝙭𝙘𝙚𝙡𝙡𝙚𝙣𝙘𝙚, 𝘼 𝙁𝙪𝙩𝙪𝙧𝙚 𝙤𝙛 𝙄𝙢𝙥𝙖𝙘𝙩]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, August 17, 2025**
Gordon College is proud to announce that the Philippine Society of Customs Administration Students (PSCAS) Gordon College Chapter soared to new heights at the PSCAS National Awards on August 16, 2025, at Wind Residences, Tagaytay City!
PSCAS GC Chapter was honored with the most prestigious award: Top Performing PSCAS Chapter!
This incredible achievement is a testament to our dedication to excellence and unwavering commitment to our community.
We also brought home a constellation of awards, including Most Outstanding in:
\* Community Impact & Civic Engagement
\* Leadership & Institutional Development Projects
\* Specialized Customs Training & Webinar Programs
And we were recognized as Outstanding in:
\* Academic Excellence & Professional Development
\* Career Preparation & Skills Development
\* Culture, Arts & Wellness Promotion
\* Environmental Advocacy & Sustainability
\* Student Engagement & Community Building Initiatives
\* Student Support & Mentorship Initiatives
We want to give a special shout-out to two of our very own who stood out among the best students in the country:
\* Kris Rean Agaton was named the Top 1 Most Outstanding BSCA Student of the Philippines 2025.
\* Renmmelle Kyle Cerilles was named among the top 3 most outstanding BSCA Students in the Philippines in 2025.
Your hard work, leadership, and passion have made a mark, and we couldn’t be prouder of your achievements.
This incredible success belongs to every member, officer, and adviser who contributed their time and talent to make our chapter shine.

# Moving UP 2023
[Image: Moving UP 2023]
[Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/extension/) [RDCES](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/rdces/) [Community Extension](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/community-extension/)
**Wednesday, July 12, 2023**
The 13 sixth-grade graduates of Iram II Elementary School received a generous gift from the GC Community, represented by the GC CESU. The gift consisted of new unisex backpacks and essential school supplies like notebooks, ballpoint pens, paper, pencils, rulers, and erasers, preparing them for the upcoming academic year. Additionally, they were provided with a kilogram of rice, canned foods, noodles, soap, alcohol, and face masks, alleviating their household expenses for one to two days. These items were collected during the Moving-Up donation initiative, which saw enthusiastic participation from the entire GC community, including administrative staff, faculty, students, and student organizations.
Moreover, 19 kindergarten graduates were recognized for their dedication and hard work in their learning journey and were also presented with essential goods as tokens of appreciation.

# Starbooks Project MOU Signing Ceremony
[Image: Starbooks Project MOU Signing Ceremony]
[LIMC](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/tag/limc/) [News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Sunday, July 15, 2018**
Gordon College, with other local HEIs in Olongapo City, and Starbooks project of the Department of Science and Technology and Department of Education last January 10, 2018 signed a Memorandum of Understanding that will allow these institutions to work together on a project that will help educate students and faculty about new technologies.
The project aims to improve research, education and development through the use of digital books.

# DISINFECTION OF GORDON COLLEGE MAIN AND ANNEX BUILDINGS DUE TO RISING CASES OF INFLUENZA
[Image: DISINFECTION OF GORDON COLLEGE MAIN AND ANNEX BUILDINGS DUE TO RISING CASES OF INFLUENZA]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Friday, October 17, 2025**
Due to the rising cases of Influenza-like illnesses, the City Health Office conducts disinfection procedures at 1:00pm, October 17, Gordon College Main and Annex Building.
With this, Face-to-face classes shifted to online mode in the afternoon and will resume the following day, October 18.
Students and campus personnel who are experiencing symptoms of flu are advised to wear a face mask to ensure safety.| Jasmine Zeah Y. Llagas /The FOREFRONT

# CHTM Sharks sealed the set against CEAS Mentors in Men’s Singles
[Image: CHTM Sharks sealed the set against CEAS Mentors in Men’s Singles]
[News](https://gordoncollege.edu.ph/w3/category/news/)
**Wednesday, September 17, 2025**
TRICKSHOT COVERED COURT—The College of Hospitality and Tourism Management (CHTM) Sharks bagged the gold again during the men’s badminton singles championship match, 21-6, defeating the College of Education, Arts and Sciences (CEAS) Mentors.
With his outstanding performance, Kryztofer Matias Basa of CHTM Sharks ended the finals with two straight sets, leaving no chance for his opponent to recover.
In an interview, Basa shared that he already expected the victory as he had once played with a stronger player before.
“‘Yu‘n pa yung ginamit ko na motivation para magchampion ulit yung CHTM,” he said when asked about being pressured to defend the previous win of CHTM last SIKLAB.
He also expressed his joy in playing with passion and humility. “Iniisip ko lang is maging humble, and…sportsmanship,” he added.
Moreover, the College of Computer Studies secured the bronze medal, while the College of Business and Accountancy and the College of Allied Health got the 4th and 5th place, respectively. | via Jeliza Tadena/The FOREFRONT
